name: OpenCode Model Router
tagline: Quota-aware subagent routing and local workflow tracing for OpenCode
description:
A local, deterministic router for OpenCode 2.x. It wraps the existing subagent tool and selects a model per invocation based on seven specialist roles, four difficulty tiers, importance, context size and modality, while keeping Plan and Build on their normal primary models. Quota comes from the existing AI Usage service instead of a second provider poller.

The router records durable SQLite reservations, enforces per-account and global concurrency limits, applies cooldowns, and fails closed when quota, identity or context checks cannot be satisfied. It also provides an authenticated local API, read-only MCP tools, a systemd user service, and workflow tracing with redacted JSON/Mermaid exports and a static HTML/SVG lifeline timeline. Paid Opus and Kimi dispatch remain locked behind a separate approval mechanism.
purpose: To delegate work across multiple model providers without oversubscribing subscription quotas, leaking credentials or silently changing the user's primary model.
strengths: Selects models per subagent call using role, tier, importance, context size and modality
Checks every applicable quota window separately and fails closed on unknown, stale or exhausted quotas
Uses durable SQLite reservations, per-account concurrency caps, cooldowns and a global limit
Reuses the AI Usage collector for authoritative quota instead of polling providers twice
Enforces critic family independence and original-session provenance for reviews
Exposes read-only MCP tools plus redacted JSON, Mermaid and static timeline exports
Installs additively and includes a tested disable/rollback path
limitations: The SQLite ledger coordinates managed tasks on one machine, not a cluster
Subscription reservations are estimated percentage points, not exact token capacity
Paid Opus and Kimi dispatch are intentionally locked in this release
Depends on the AI Usage service for fresh quota observations
installation:
# Install dependencies and the additive local integration
bun install
npm run install:local

# Start the systemd user service
systemctl --user start opencode-model-router.service
systemctl --user status opencode-model-router.service
usage:
# Inspect routing state
bun src/cli.ts status

# Delegate with optional routing metadata
{
  "agent": "reviewer",
  "description": "Review transaction handling",
  "routing": {
    "tier": "HARD",
    "importance": "high",
    "inputTokens": 30000,
    "outputTokens": 8000
  }
}

# Export a recorded workflow timeline
bun src/cli.ts workflow <sessionID> --timeline --out ~/.local/share/opencode-model-router/exports/timeline.html
roadmap: Add a trusted approval and monetary reservation mechanism for paid models
Improve tokenizer integration to reduce conservative input rejection
Expand measured performance data beyond short diagnostic probes
Harden coordination beyond the local single-host ledger
